key_insight: O²LaF proposes reusing one pretrained video diffusion transformer as the starting point for two tasks: inferring latent actions from visual changes and predicting changes from those actions. The central idea is to transfer learned video knowledge instead of learning dynamics largely from scratch.
problem_solved: Videos show what changes but rarely label the actions responsible. Learning these hidden actions requires understanding dynamics, which existing approaches often learn largely from scratch.
method: Initialize both inverse- and forward-dynamics models from the same pretrained video diffusion transformer (DiT).
Use inverse dynamics to infer latent actions from visual transitions.
Use forward dynamics to model action-conditioned transitions, drawing on the same pretrained video prior.
impact: The approach offers practitioners a way to repurpose video-generation pretraining for self-supervised latent action learning. The provided abstract is incomplete, so performance gains and implementation details cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: A shared pretrained video DiT branching into inverse- and forward-dynamics models, labeled “One prior, two dynamics.”
An inverse-dynamics diagram: before frame + after frame → inferred latent action.
A forward-dynamics diagram: current frame + latent action → predicted next frame.
A side-by-side schematic contrasting learning dynamics from scratch with initializing from a pretrained video prior.
paper_title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
paper_authors: Yuxin Jiang, Wenqiang Sun, Jiaqi Li, Yuchao Gu, Lvmin Zhang
